issues.description: The golden/expert submission is rejected by the evaluator, which is the core blocking defect. The differential harness shows the golden run fails FR4 and SR5 due to overly aggressive regex-based address-mention scanning of the free-text 'evidence' field. The heuristic in find_address_mentions_in_text (matching any bare 3-digit 0/1 sequence via the fallback regex, plus sentence splitting on '.', ';', '\n') picks up incidental binary-looking substrings or address enumerations in the evidence prose (e.g. describing the full 8-address sweep or bit-width values) and misclassifies them as blanket/fabricated anomaly claims, even though the golden report correctly scopes trojan_present, trigger_condition, affected_outputs, and suspect_nets to address 011 only.
issues.evidence: golden_run.stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: FR4: evidence text appears to claim anomalous/Trojan-affected behavior at address(es) other than the reported trigger address 011: [000, 001, 010, 100, 101, 110, 111]' and '[TEST] FAIL: SR5: evidence text claims anomalous behavior at address(es) [010, 100, 111] ... only [011] is anomalous'

issues.description: Because the golden solution fails, mutation_score is 0.0 and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 per the validation report; the benchmark cannot currently distinguish correct from incorrect submissions reliably for FR4/SR5, undermining the entire grading pipeline despite otherwise reasonable vulnerable-run behavior (correctly rejects the naive baseline).
issues.evidence: validation report: 'mutation_score': 0.0, 'mutation_status': 'blocked_by_differential', 'requirement_discrimination_coverage_score': 0.0, issue 'golden_rejected': 'evaluate.py rejects the expert golden solution (PASS expected)'

issues.description: The evidence-text address-mention heuristic (find_address_mentions_in_text) uses an overly broad bare-triplet regex fallback that will false-positive on any coincidental 3-digit 0/1 substring appearing anywhere in free text near an anomaly keyword within the same sentence, making FR4 and SR5 fragile and prone to rejecting legitimate, well-scoped evidence descriptions in general (not just in this one golden instance).
issues.evidence: regex: r'(?<![01])([01]{3})(?![01])' applied to arbitrary evidence prose, combined with naive sentence splitting and keyword co-occurrence in the same sentence

recommendations: Fix or remove the overly broad bare-triplet fallback regex in find_address_mentions_in_text (r'(?<![01])([01]{3})(?![01])') that spuriously matches incidental 3-character 0/1 substrings in free-text evidence; restrict address-mention detection to more explicit forms like 3'b011, addr=011, or quoted "011" tokens to avoid false positives.

Re-tune the FR4/SR5 sentence-level anomaly-keyword co-occurrence heuristic so it does not trigger on the golden report's evidence text; validate against the actual golden trojan_report.json evidence field content before finalizing the check.
Re-run the differential harness after the regex fix to confirm the golden submission now exits 0 with all 9 requirement ids PASS, and that the naive baseline still fails on SR1-SR4 as shown.
Consider adding a golden-submission regression test to the evaluator's own test suite so future changes to the evidence-text heuristics cannot silently regress golden acceptance again.
Once the golden-acceptance defect is fixed, re-verify mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score to ensure they rise above the current blocked/zero state.
